key_insight: The paper partitions the turbulent kinetic energy budget in wall-bounded flows into distinct scaling patches, each governed by a different dominant balance and scaling law.
engineering_relevance: This unified patch-based scaling can improve interpretation and modeling of near-wall, intermediate, and outer-layer turbulence across Reynolds numbers.
method: Apply scaling-patch analysis to the TKE budget equation in wall-bounded turbulence.
Use viscous diffusion–dissipation balance to define the near-wall sublayer and Kolmogorov-length thickness.
Introduce inner, meso, and outer scalings using peak TKE production and Prandtl mixing-length ideas.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical framework validated by comparing the TKE budget structure across wall-bounded-flow regions and Reynolds numbers, emphasizing improved collapse under the proposed scalings.
watch_item: The patch boundaries and scaling choices may be flow-regime dependent, so extending the framework to other wall-bounded configurations may require careful recalibration.
paper_title: Scaling patch analysis of turbulent kinetic energy budget equation in wall-bounded flows
